rv.q: We’re always entertained, frequently laughing — at the same time, as in certain Wes Anderson movies, there’s something in the extra-stylish surface that keeps deeper feelings at bay.
Adams keeps all those balls in the air with an offhand elegance that makes the whole thing seem much easier than it ought to.

cn.t: Reddick's ambitious, genre-blending play divides critics with its tonal slipperiness and overstuffed plot, though most praise its Lynchian direction, strong performances, and striking 80s texture even when questioning how it all coheres.
